_comment: Authored content for the roadmap page. Statuses are NOT stored here: tools/build-roadmap.mjs computes them from EVIDENCE_REGISTER.md, DECISIONS.md and the files named below, and writes frontend/static/data/roadmap.json.

phases.title: Application foundation
phases.summary: A storefront that runs with no AWS account, so a failure in the cloud can be blamed on the infrastructure and not on the code.
phases.objective: Build the application on SQLite first, with the same code paths that will later talk to RDS.

tasks.text: Python backend in backend/, server-rendered frontend in frontend/
tasks.detail: Installs and passes its tests from a clean virtual environment; CSS, fonts, JavaScript and images load in a real browser.

tasks.text: Configuration through environment variables; production refuses weak secrets and SQLite
SQLAlchemy models, per-size stock, persistence on SQLite
tasks.detail: Orders survive an application restart in the tests.

tasks.text: The same code on MySQL (RDS): connection, TLS option, schema creation
tasks.detail: URL building and the TLS option are unit tested; no run against a live MySQL yet.

validation: pytest passes from a clean virtual environment (E-022).
The browser test confirms the stylesheet, fonts, scripts and images load from frontend/static (E-016).
A demo order is written and read back on SQLite (E-015).
notInScope: Customer accounts and login. Nothing is built, so there is no authentication or authorization to verify. An order is visible only to the browser session that placed it.

phases.title: Security design
phases.summary: Decide where each control lives (application code, network, IAM) and mark which ones exist today.
phases.objective: Every control has an owner layer and a status; none is claimed without a test or a screenshot.

tasks.text: Server-side prices and stock, input validation, CSRF, parameterised SQL, strict CSP, safe errors
tasks.detail: Each control has a test that fails when it is removed.

tasks.text: Dependency vulnerability scan
tasks.detail: One manual pip-audit run; repeat before publishing.

tasks.text: Secrets read from Secrets Manager, not from code or user data
tasks.detail: Loader written and tested with a fake client; nothing read from AWS yet.

tasks.text: Security-group chain (alb-sg, app-sg, db-sg) and no SSH
tasks.detail: Designed; the rules do not exist in AWS yet.

tasks.text: Instance role limited to two secrets; database user with DML rights only
tasks.detail: Designed; waiting for the AWS build.

tasks.text: Security design written, with the status of every control

validation: Mutation check: deliberately breaking six behaviours makes tests fail each time (E-015).
AWS controls are checked by behaviour, not by screenshots of settings: a failed connection from the internet (E-007).
notInScope: HTTPS, WAF and rate limiting. Listed as known limitations.

phases.title: AWS architecture design
phases.summary: A three-tier layout across two Availability Zones, written down with its trade-offs. This phase is design only.
phases.objective: A plan specific enough to build from the Console, including how it fails.

tasks.text: Network plan: one VPC, six subnets, route tables, security-group chain
Decision log with the alternatives that were rejected
Diagram: static image and an animated traffic-flow view

validation: Subnet CIDRs, ports and group names in the animated diagram match docs/architecture.md (checked by tools/check-docs.mjs).
Failure behaviour is written down: an AZ-a failure likely means an outage, because the NAT gateway and the database are both in AZ a.
notInScope: Route 53, CloudFront, WAF, Multi-AZ RDS, a NAT gateway per AZ. They are production steps, not part of this design.

phases.title: Manual AWS implementation
phases.summary: Create every resource by hand in the Console, one checkpoint at a time, with a screenshot for each.
phases.objective: Build the design and capture real evidence at each gate before moving on.

tasks.text: CP0: budget alert, root MFA, non-root identity, Region chosen
CP1: VPC, six subnets, internet gateway, route tables
CP2: security groups
CP3: RDS MySQL in private subnets, encrypted
CP4: IAM role, NAT gateway, launch template, first instance through Session Manager
CP5: target group, load balancer, two instances

validation: Each checkpoint's gate in docs/checkpoints/ or the RDS and deployment guides is met.
Screenshots are redacted and saved under screenshots/01 to 05, then recorded in the evidence register.
notInScope: Terraform, CloudFormation, CI/CD, containers. The build is deliberately manual.

phases.title: Testing and verification
phases.summary: Show that the parts behave as designed, not just that they are configured. A healthy target group is not a working checkout.
phases.objective: Every security and availability claim is backed by an observed result.

tasks.text: Automated application tests
Real-browser checks: flows, keyboard order, mobile layout, static assets
Configuration checks: clean-room install, ignore rules, no private files
A demo order through the load balancer lands in RDS
Database unreachable from the internet; instances not directly reachable
Terminate one instance; the service survives and is replaced
Defects recorded with their causes and fixes
tasks.detail: Local defects are logged. The AWS issue log is empty because nothing has been built.

validation: A claim is VERIFIED only with an evidence file and an observed result (docs/project/EVIDENCE_REGISTER.md).
Each test states what it proves and what it does not.
notInScope: Load testing, penetration testing, MySQL concurrency tests. Not planned for this project.

phases.title: Final review
phases.summary: Re-run the reviews with real AWS evidence, check the cost, tear everything down, and update the write-ups.
phases.objective: Leave a repository where every claim matches its evidence and nothing keeps billing.

tasks.text: Review passes on the local build (code, security, documentation, interface)
Case study, notebook and summary written for the local build
Re-review and update the write-ups with real AWS results
tasks.detail: Cannot start before the AWS build has evidence.

tasks.text: Cost check, teardown in order, billing reviewed the next day

validation: Resource lists are empty for every service in the build Region (E-014).
README, case study and notebook state only what the register supports.
